html:
John Garang was the leader of the Sudan People's Liberation Movement and its army, which fought the government of Sudan from 1983 to 2005.

A Dinka from near Bor, he fought with the Anyanya rebels, then joined the Sudanese army and earned a doctorate in agricultural economics in the United States. Sent to put down the Bor mutiny in 1983, he joined it instead and led the second civil war.

Unlike many southerners, he called for a united, secular and democratic Sudan rather than secession. He signed the Comprehensive Peace Agreement and became first vice president of Sudan in July 2005, but died three weeks later when his helicopter crashed. His death left the south to leaders who chose independence for South Sudan.
